section: Parliamentary devices - Question Hour, Zero Hour, motions (adjournment, no-confidence, censure, calling attention)

accepted.s: A resolution/no-confidence motion directed against Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla was recently disposed of by:
o: Casting vote of the Deputy Speaker
accepted.x: The resolution/no-confidence motion against Speaker Om Birla was dismissed by voice vote.
accepted.tq: Use the direct event-detail approach and distinguish the voting method from other parliamentary voting procedures.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha under Article 94(c):
1. The resolution requires a majority of all the then members of the House.
2. A notice of fourteen days is required.
3. The notice must be supported by at least fifty members.
4. The procedure is governed by Rules 200–203 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Article 94(c), the fourteen-day notice requirement, support of fifty members and Lok Sabha Rules 200–203 govern the removal procedure.
accepted.tq: Check each procedural requirement separately, especially the constitutional provision, notice period, numerical support and relevant Rules.

accepted.s: Which Article of the Constitution is associated with the removal of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
accepted.x: Article 94(c) provides for vacation and removal from the office of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Use article-number discrimination among closely related parliamentary provisions.

accepted.s: A privilege notice was moved in the Rajya Sabha against which Union Minister in May 2026?
accepted.x: A privilege notice was moved in the Rajya Sabha against the Union Education Minister on 20 May 2026.
accepted.tq: Match the parliamentary device with the correct House and authority involved.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following parliamentary developments in chronological order:
A. Introduction of Zero Hour
B. Introduction of the Calling Attention device
C. First meeting of the PAC for 2026–27
D. Privilege notice against the Union Education Minister in the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: The Calling Attention device dates to 1954, Zero Hour to 1962, the privilege notice to May 2026, and the PAC’s first meeting to 26 May 2026.
accepted.tq: Fix the first two historical years and then distinguish the two events occurring in 2026.

accepted.s: The first meeting of the Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27 was held under the chairmanship of:
o: The Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: The PAC for 2026–27 held its first meeting under K.C. Venugopal.
accepted.tq: Identify the person associated with the current functioning of the committee rather than its constitutional or procedural role.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary committee functioning in 2026:
1. The average attendance in the 16 Departmentally Related Standing Committees and the Public Accounts Committee was 53%.
2. Five meetings were postponed for lack of quorum.
3. The Public Accounts Committee held no meeting during 2026–27.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The PAC held its first meeting for 2026–27, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the false statement by checking the numerical attendance figure, the quorum-related postponements and the existence of the PAC meeting.

accepted.s: In the 17th Lok Sabha, what proportion of Bills were referred to parliamentary committees?
accepted.x: Only 16% of Bills in the 17th Lok Sabha were referred to committees; the corresponding figure for the 15th Lok Sabha was 71%.
accepted.tq: Separate the figures belonging to the 17th and 15th Lok Sabhas instead of selecting the larger comparison value.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares the referral of Bills to parliamentary committees in India and the United Kingdom?
o: Every Indian Bill is examined by committees of both Houses, whereas UK Bills are rarely referred.
Fewer than one-fifth of UK Bills are referred, whereas every Indian Bill is referred.
Every UK Bill is examined by committees of both Houses, whereas in India fewer than one-fifth of Bills are referred to committees.
Both countries refer all Bills to committees of both Houses.
accepted.x: Every UK Bill is examined by committees of both Houses. In India, fewer than one-fifth of Bills are referred to committees.
accepted.tq: Keep the country-wise comparison in the correct direction and watch for the reversal of ‘every’ and ‘fewer than one-fifth’.

accepted.s: Question Hour in Parliament functioned for what proportion of its scheduled time, according to the cited assessment?
accepted.x: Question Hour ran for only 60% of its scheduled time in the cited assessment.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Question Hour utilisation figure from the committee attendance and Bill-referral percentages.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly is correct?
o: Biometric attendance was introduced only for members of Parliament from the Budget Session of 2026.
Biometric attendance for MLAs was introduced from the Budget Session of 2026.
Biometric attendance for MLAs was introduced from the Monsoon Session of 2025.
Biometric attendance was introduced for MLAs from the Winter Session of 2026.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh introduced biometric attendance for MLAs from its Budget Session in 2026.
accepted.tq: Use precise state-level identification by checking the institution, year and legislative session together.
